clips.title: Wear Sunglasses After Night Shift to Sleep Better
clips.text: Slip on a pair of dark sunglasses the moment you step outside. And you block most of that signal. The result. Your body still thinks it's night, melatonin rises on schedule, and you fall asleep faster once you're in bed. It's the cheapest sleep intervention I know, just a dollar ten pair of shades. And it works because light is the master switch for the circadian system. So the takeaway is simple, protect your eyes from morning light and you protect your sleep pressure.

clips.title: Use the Half‑Flip to Recover Faster After Night Shifts
clips.text: The gentler approach call it a half -flip. Is to sleep for a short -core block. Say 3 hours right after the shift, then stay up for a few hours, get bright light. And finally go to bed at a reasonable evening hour. This splits the adjustment into two smaller jumps instead of one massive leap. And most people report feeling functional within 48 hours, instead of a week. So the half -flip gives the clock a manageable step. And you avoid the brutal all -day wakefulness that wrecks recovery.
